If a point P divides the line joining A(x1, y1) and B(x2, y2) internally in the ratio m:n, its coordinates are: ((mx2 + nx1)/(m + n), (my2 + ny1)/(m + n)).

t.title: To Make a Mixture from Two Mixtures

en.value:
Shortcut Trick

When the profit amount is equal to the loss amount, the Cost Price (CP) is the exact average of the two Selling Prices.

CP = (1680 + 1420) ÷ 2

CP = 3100 ÷ 2 = 1550

To gain a 20% profit, multiply the CP by the 1.2 multiplying factor.

Target SP = 1550 × 1.2 = 1860

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1,860.

Alternate Method

Given:

Selling Price (SP1) for profit = Rs. 1680

Selling Price (SP2) for loss = Rs. 1420

Target Profit Percentage = 20%

Formula Used:

Profit = SP − CP

Loss = CP − SP

SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100

Calculations:

According to the given condition, Profit earned = Loss incurred

⇒ SP1 − CP = CP − SP2

⇒ 1680 − CP = CP − 1420

⇒ CP + CP = 1680 + 1420

⇒ 2 × CP = 3100

⇒ CP = 3100 ÷ 2 = Rs. 1550

Now, we need to find the new Selling Price to gain 20% profit on this Cost Price.

⇒ New SP = CP × (100 + 20) ÷ 100

⇒ New SP = 1550 × 120 ÷ 100

⇒ New SP = 1550 × 1.20 = Rs. 1860

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1,860.

Additional Information

Equal Profit and Loss Percentages

When an article is sold at a profit of x% and another article is sold at a loss of x% with the identical Selling Price, there is always an overall net loss equal to (x÷10)2 %.

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a shopkeeper claims to sell items at the Cost Price but uses a false weight, Profit% = (True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight × 100.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of d1% and d2% are offered, the equivalent single discount is given by (d1 + d2 − d1×d2÷100)%.

Net increase in total marks = 99 − 9 = 90

Increase in class average = 2.25

Number of students = Net increase in total marks ÷ Increase in average

⇒ Number of students = 90 ÷ 2.25 = 40

∴ The correct answer is 40 students.

Alternate Method

Given:

Actual marks of Renu = 9

Wrongly entered marks = 99

Increase in average marks of the class = 2.25

Formula Used:

Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations

Calculations:

Let the total number of students in the class be n and the correct sum of marks of all students be S.

⇒ Correct Average = S ÷ n

⇒ Incorrect Sum of marks = S − 9 + 99 = S + 90

⇒ Incorrect Average = (S + 90) ÷ n = (S ÷ n) + (90 ÷ n)

We know that: Incorrect Average − Correct Average = 2.25

⇒ [(S ÷ n) + (90 ÷ n)] − (S ÷ n) = 2.25

⇒ 90 ÷ n = 2.25

⇒ n = 90 ÷ 2.25

⇒ n = 9000 ÷ 225

⇒ n = 40

∴ The correct answer is 40 students.

Additional Information

Concept of Deviation in Averages

When a value is replaced by a larger value, the net increase is distributed equally among all observations. Thus, Change in Average = Difference in values ÷ Total Number of observations.

Combined Average

If two groups have sizes n1 and n2 with averages A1 and A2, then the combined average is (n1 × A1 + n2 × A2) ÷ (n1 + n2).

Change due to Addition

If a new observation is added and the average increases, the new value is greater than the initial average. New Value = Old Average + (Total new elements × Increase in Average).

Shortcut Trick

The amount saved corresponds directly to the discount percentage given.

25% of Marked Price → Rs. 20

100% of Marked Price → 20 × 4 = Rs. 80

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 80.

Alternate Method

Given:

Discount percentage = 25%

Amount saved (Discount value) = Rs. 20

Formula Used:

Discount = (Discount% ÷ 100) × Marked Price

Calculations:

Let the price of the shirt before the discount (Marked Price) be x.

⇒ 25% of x = 20

⇒ (25 ÷ 100) × x = 20

⇒ (1 ÷ 4) × x = 20

⇒ x = 20 × 4

⇒ x = 80

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 80.

Additional Information

Marked Price (MP)

It is the price printed on the article. All discounts are exclusively calculated on the Marked Price, not the Cost Price.

Selling Price (SP) after Discount

SP = MP − Discount, or SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount percentage is (a + b − a × b ÷ 100)%.
